one_line_contribution: When a stored agent trajectory is reused by a different backbone, the transferable part is the action-observation sequence and the lost part is the writer's reasoning text, so a zero-cost deterministic parser that deletes the thought slot recovers the cross-backbone deficit, the harm tracks who authored the thoughts rather than who authored the actions, and a model-aware LLM rewriter buys nothing over the strip at matched tokens.
closest_prior_work: Two verified threats, neither fatal. (1) arXiv:2605.30723, 'Skill is Not One-Size-Fits-All: Model-Aware Skill Alignment for LLM Agents' (verified via the literature command, S2, 2026-05-29, 2 citations) already establishes the premise the proposal builds on -- skill utility is model-dependent and reusing one formulation across backbones is wrong -- and supplies the rewriter the proposal wants to beat. It does not decompose an item into thought/action/scaffold and does not run an action-only strip as a baseline, so the strip-vs-rewriter comparison is genuinely open; but this means the proposal's contribution is an ablation and a missing baseline for an existing paper, which is a real but modest increment. (2) The sharper threat to the mechanism is arXiv:2509.23196, 'From Harm to Help: Turning Reasoning In-Context Demos into Assets for Reasoning LMs' (verified, S2, 2025-09-27), which already reports that reasoning traces inside in-context demonstrations HARM reasoning LMs and fixes it by converting demos into insights (I2S/I2S+) across open- and closed-source models. 'Foreign reasoning text in a demonstration is the harmful component' is therefore not new as a phenomenon; what is new here is localizing it to a writer x reader interaction with the author of the thoughts swapped at fixed actions (F3/F5) inside an agent-memory store. Note also that I2S+ is an existence proof that an LLM conversion step CAN beat the raw demos, which is exactly P3's falsifier -- the proposal should cite it and explain why its rewriter is expected to fail where I2S succeeded. Parametric cousins, all verified: arXiv:2603.13260 'Explain in Your Own Words' (token-selective dual KD, 13 cit), arXiv:2509.22230 'In Their Own Words: Reasoning Traces Tailored for Small Models', arXiv:2512.20908 (provenance tracing in reasoning distillation, 7 cit), arXiv:2306.14050 (SCoTD, 241 cit); the proposal correctly identifies these as the training-time analog of F3 and they do not pre-empt the in-context form. Adjacent and uncited: arXiv:2604.01029 'Revision or Re-Solving? Decomposing Second-Pass Gains in Multi-LLM Pipelines' (verified, 2 cit) decomposes multi-LLM second-pass gains into re-solving, scaffold and content components -- the same decompose-the-gain-into-components move in a neighbouring setting.
strongest_objection: The plan cannot decide its own headline at the power it has, and it says so. Every pass/fail criterion separates a predicted value from a falsifier by 2 to 3 net points (P1: +5 vs +3; P2: +2 vs +4; P3: +2 vs +4; P4b: 2 vs 5) against pooled half-widths of +/-1.2 to +/-2.6. Those half-widths are manufactured by two scalings of Measurement C's single measured number (+/-5.25 paired at 274 games x 2 seeds), and both scalings assume variance this design does not have. First, sqrt(2/S) over seeds: seeds re-run the SAME fixed 274 validation games, so extra seeds shrink only the decoding-stochasticity component, while the between-game component -- which is precisely what the pre-registered game-cluster bootstrap keeps inside the interval -- does not shrink at all. Six seeds therefore cannot deliver +/-3.0 per cell if the paired contrast at two seeds is +/-5.25 and most of that width is between-game. Second, 1/sqrt(cells): the six cross cells share the same 274 games and, within a writer, the same retrieved items and the same injected strings, so they are strongly positively correlated and pooling does not buy sqrt(6). The proposal concedes the second point and pre-registers a fallback -- 'if the realized pooled width exceeds 1.5x the design figure, per-cell criteria are reported as the result' -- but per-cell widths are +/-3.0 to +/-4.3, which cannot distinguish Delta_strip = +5 from the +3 falsifier in any cell. The pre-registered fallback is thus a design in which P1, P2, P3 and P4(b) are all undecidable, and nothing in the plan can add power: ALFWorld's validation split caps N at 274 games, and the episode budget is already 60,300. The likely paper is six directional point estimates with overlapping intervals and a title that asserts a decomposition the intervals do not support. A secondary form of the same objection: Gate 0, which establishes that there IS a cross-backbone deficit to decompose, is explicitly 'framing only' and P1-P6 run regardless -- so the paper is guaranteed to be written even if the phenomenon its title names does not exist, and the pre-registered fallback framing ('harm-and-removal rather than deficit recovery') quietly abandons 'the non-transferable part of cross-backbone agent experience' while keeping the headline.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Re-derive the noise model empirically instead of by scaling. Measurement C's runs are on disk: bootstrap the realized paired k3-static3 contrast at one seed versus two to measure the actual seed-reducible fraction of the +/-5.25, and jointly bootstrap two cells that share games to measure the cell-cell correlation. Set seeds and cells from those two numbers, and pre-register margins that survive them. (2) If +/-1.2 is unreachable -- it probably is -- restate P1 as a within-pool paired interaction rather than a pooled difference of pooled means: for each writer pool W, compute Delta_strip(W->R) - Delta_strip(W->W) on the same items and the same games, which is a paired quantity with the pool-quality confound differenced out (as pooled, the interaction compares cells built from different pools, so 'E's thoughts are simply worse/longer than Q's, and stripping bad thoughts helps everyone' is not excluded by the current estimand). Then a sign test over the six within-pool interactions is a criterion the design can actually meet. (3) Add the token-matched irrelevant-thought placebo described below. (4) Take the entailment check's P6 fix verbatim: pre-register one same-backbone F6 cell and one cross F6 cell at the SMALLEST Phase-A verbatim deficit, so 'thoughts carry the procedure' has a cell where it could appear; selecting both F6 cells on largest deficit selects on an outcome-correlated criterion. (5) Drop P4(b) as a prediction or give it an arm -- as written DoD = (P4a - P1a) + P1b up to the F5-self offset and adds no evidence. (6) Use the on-disk expert pool as the highest-powered positive control for the authorship claim: X is already stripped and its gain for Q is measured (+17.2 over static3, CI +/-5), so X actions plus foreign teacher-forced thoughts versus X in F2 form tests 'adding foreign thoughts destroys transfer' in the one cell where the baseline is known rather than assumed. That arm is cheap, uses data already collected, and would carry the paper even if the Q/E/G matrix comes back noisy. (7) Fix the abstract's 'byte-identical injected strings': the retrieved items are shared, the serialized context is not, since F1r/F2 re-render into each reader's scaffold template.
missing_baseline: A token-matched irrelevant-thought placebo: the writer's own thoughts taken from a DIFFERENT episode (or a different task type), spliced onto the retrieved actions at matched per-step length. Without it, 'the harm follows the author of the thoughts' (P4, P5) is not separated from 'the harm follows any thought text that was not generated for these actions'. F5-E and F5-G are teacher-forced rationalizations of action sequences their authors would not have chosen, so foreign authorship and post-hoc incoherence vary together, and the single F5-self offset arm calibrates post-hoc-ness only in the matched-author case; F6 (thoughts only) is a content placebo, not a length-matched noise placebo, and blind1 is a wrong-type ITEM placebo measured under k=0 in a different experiment and explicitly not re-run. The brief's own binding rule ('token- and rate-matched placebos', 'contamination arms are manufactured, gated and positively controlled') asks for exactly this arm. Second omission a reviewer will name: an F2-at-matched-tokens arm. F2 deletes tokens and holds k=3, so the practical recommendation ('strip the thoughts') frees budget that a competitor would spend on more items; F2 at k=5-7 to match F1r's token count would show whether the strip's advantage survives when the reader could instead have had more demonstrations, and it is the arm that decides whether the result is a claim about thoughts or a claim about context budget.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is above average for this round -- it names the channel (s2cli.py, S2 + HF, both 'ok'), states that WebSearch was unavailable, reports three query classes (recent mechanism, home literature, closest named method) and returns IDs rather than assertions -- and I verified the IDs it leans on: 2605.30723 (S2, 2026-05-29, 2 cit, exactly the Model-Aware Skill Alignment paper described), 2608.06880 SkillAligner, 2606.01311 SkillAdaptor (9 cit), 2606.01139 SkillRevise, 2603.13260 'Explain in Your Own Words' (13 cit), 2512.20908 (7 cit), 2509.23574 MoRSD, 2306.14050 SCoTD (241 cit), 2608.24232 TRACE and 2608.10232 FACT -- the last two are a reasoning-safety benchmark and a world-action model respectively, i.e. false positives the proposal listed without noting that they are off-topic. 2605.11032 failed a direct id lookup and I recovered it only through a search: 'Portable Agent Memory: A Protocol for Cryptographically-Verified Memory Transfer Across Heterogeneous AI Agents' (S2, 2026-05-10, 3 cit) -- verified, though it is a protocol/SDK artifact, so the Related Work claim that its rehydration step is a serious uncompared adaptation baseline is weaker than stated. My own queries, all answered by the literature command (channel (a); WebSearch unavailable in this session, WebFetch never used): (i) recent, 'removing reasoning traces from in-context demonstrations improves cross-model transfer action-only' -> 2509.23196, 2509.22230, 2606.00642, 2604.01161, 2512.20908, 2510.11545, 2509.13237 -- the first two are the notable misses; (ii) all-years, 'chain-of-thought demonstrations from a different model hurt in-context learning reasoning style mismatch' -> 2409.04057, 2311.09277, 2401.04925, 2410.21333, 2402.16048, nothing closer than the novelty card already showed; (iii) recent, closest named method, 'model-aware rewriter adapts retrieved skill to target backbone versus no adaptation baseline' -> 2605.30723, 2608.06880, 2606.01139, 2605.09359, 2608.03874, 2604.01029 -- confirming no strip baseline in that family and surfacing 2604.01029 as an uncited decomposition analog; (iv) recent, 'agent experience memory stores trajectories action observation only without reasoning thoughts reused by another backbone' -> 2607.28272 MemHarness, 2607.10608 'The Compliance Trap', 2608.04530 FocusMem, 2605.24468 SAM -- none decomposes a stored item into thought versus action; (v) recent, 'portable memory format protocol transfer agent memory across models rehydration' -> 2605.11032 (verification), 2608.07169, 2608.11224, 2606.05684. The material gap in the proposal's check is that its recent-mechanism query used agent/experience vocabulary and therefore missed the in-context CoT-demo-harm line: 2509.23196 reports that reasoning demonstrations harm reasoning LMs and that an LLM conversion step turns them into an asset, and 2509.22230 reports that teacher traces are distributionally misaligned for small students and must be re-authored 'in their own words'. Neither manipulates writer identity at fixed actions, neither is agentic, and neither runs a deterministic action-only strip, so the central claim is not scooped -- but the claim's premise (foreign reasoning text in context is the harmful component) is already published, and the check's conclusion 'no collision found; no new citation was added in this revision' overstates what the searches licensed. Novelty is scored on that basis: the phenomenon is known, the decomposition and the authorship swap are the new part.
